messages:
Maya T.: heads up — we just got a customer escalation (acct: AcmeAI) reporting intermittent 504s + timeouts from hosted /v1/generate over the last 30m. They say it correlates with large batch submissions from their side.
Devon R.: thanks, linking their support thread?
support-jordan: https://redwood.support/threads/ACME-778 — attached curl shows they send ~50 requests in parallel with payloads of ~1600 tokens. Customer saw 504s ~20% of calls.
Alejandra P.: :eyes: that's consistent with the gateway queue getting starved by large batches + long tail token generation. Any stack traces or gateway logs?
ops-bot: deploy: canary-serving-pool scale_event: 2026-03-17T14:02:12Z — noticed backlog spike on queue_processor (avg queue_depth 42 -> 210).
Sam (oncall): I'm on it. Reproduced locally by replaying their batch pattern against staging — saw queue growth and per-request queue_timeout hitting 30s.
Devon R.: steps to mitigate quickly? Rolling config change?
Sam (oncall): short-term: lower max_batch_size and reduce request queue window for hosted gateway routing. I'm going to push a temporary profile: max_batch_size 32 -> 16, queue_timeout 30s -> 15s. That should drop tail latency.
Maya T.: please notify Acme they can also reduce client concurrency as an immediate workaround. Jordan can you message them?
support-jordan: pinged the user with suggested client-side throttling and asked for repro artifacts. They've shared a small replay script.
Devon R.: longer-term we need to examine autoscaler policies for serving pools handling long-seq workloads. Also consider per-cust routing to dedicated smaller-batch pools.
Alejandra P.: agreed — adding action items: 1) postmortem root cause, 2) autoscaler policy tweak, 3) add per-route backpressure signals + early rejection codes (429 vs 504), 4) docs for customer batching best practices.
Sam (oncall): patch rolling now to reduce batch size and queue window, will monitor for 10min then confirm.
ops-bot: alert: hosted-gateway-queue-depth reduced to avg 18 at 2026-03-17T14:12:03Z.
Sam (oncall): early results look good, 504 rate dropped to baseline. Leaving this thread open for postmortem followup.
Maya T.: thanks. Devon/Alejandra own the postmortem writeup and action items, Sam will add mitigation notes and exact config change. Jordan continue customer comms and collect any additional repro logs.
Devon R.: will draft postmortem today — initial hypothesis: backpressure + batching + autoscaler ramp lag causing head-of-line blocking for short requests.
Alejandra P.: I'll add perf traces and kernel selection logs to the writeup. Need to decide whether to ship per-customer small-batch pools or adaptive batch sizing first.
support-jordan: Acme acknowledged mitigation and will test reduced concurrency; they requested ETA for permanent fix. I told them we'd follow up after postmortem.
Maya T.: action item checklist created in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/4321 — assign owners and ETA. Closing in-channel warroom once postmortem is filed. :thumbsup:
Devon R.: assigning: autoscaler policy (devon) due EOD+2, routing/backpressure feature spec (alejandra) due EOD+5.
Sam (oncall): note for postmortem: include exact config diff: 
```
- max_batch_size: 32
- queue_window_ms: 100
+ max_batch_size: 16
+ queue_window_ms: 50
+ queue_timeout_s: 15
```
Maya T.: great. leaving follow-up reminders. If anything regresses ping #incidents-alerts and notify SRE.
ops-bot: thread marked resolved by Sam (oncall) at 2026-03-17T14:20:00Z.
Maya T.: keeping thread open until postmortem published. Thanks everyone.
